architecture.name: qwen35-architecture-deep-dive
architecture.head_dims: Two head shapes per model. Full-attention ("Gated Attention") layers: head_dim 256 for Q/K/V, with partial rotary embedding on only the first 25% of dims (64 of 256; partial_rotary_factor 0.25). Linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) layers: linear_key_head_dim 128 and linear_value_head_dim 128 (Qwen3-Next-80B card also lists DeltaNet RoPE dimension 64). Verified anchors: Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B config.json (head_dim 256, linear_*_head_dim 128), Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct model card ("Head Dimension: 256" for gated attention, "Head Dimension: 128" for DeltaNet), and Qwen3.6-27B GGUF metadata ("Key/Value length: 256 per head") per yuriseki.com. Qwen3-Next-80B: 16 Q heads x 256; Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 27B dense: 24 Q heads x 256.
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Full-attention layers: qk_dim == v_dim == 256 (no MLA-style 576/512 divergence); the divergence within the head is rotary coverage - only 64/256 dims (25%) are RoPE'd, the remaining 192 pass through unrotated, and Q/K get head_dim-wide RMSNorm (q_norm/k_norm in vLLM qwen3_next.py). Linear-attention layers: per-head k=128 and v=128 are equal, but the K/V projection widths diverge via head COUNT: linear_num_key_heads 16 (K width 2048) vs linear_num_value_heads 48 (V width 6144) on the 27B dense models, and 16 K vs 32 V (V width 4096 = hidden_size) on Qwen3-Next-80B. On 27B neither K nor V width equals hidden_size 5120. Tuple view: full layers (q,k,v) = (256,256,256) with 64-dim rotary; linear layers (k,v) = (128,128) with head-count asymmetry.
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B: num_attention_heads 16, num_key_value_heads 2 -> GQA 8:1. Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8-27B dense: num_attention_heads 24, num_key_value_heads 4 -> GQA 6:1 (verified in Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B config.json and in Qwen3.6-27B GGUF metadata: "24 query heads, 4 KV heads, a 6:1 GQA ratio"). KV cache per full-attention layer per token = 2 * KV_heads * 256 elements (1024 for 80B, 2048 for 27B), stored only in 1 of every 4 layers.
architecture.hybrid_pattern: 3:1 Gated DeltaNet (linear attention) : full attention, expressed as full_attention_interval 4: layer_types[i] = "linear_attention" unless (i+1) % 4 == 0 -> "full_attention" (default pattern in vLLM Qwen3NextConfig and Qwen3_5TextConfig). Qwen3-Next-80B: 48 layers = 36 linear + 12 full, described by Qwen as "12 * (3 * (Gated DeltaNet -> MoE) -> 1 * (Gated Attention -> MoE))". Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8-27B: 64 layers = 48 linear + 16 full (GGUF metadata: full_attention_interval=4; yuriseki.com: "48 layers use Gated DeltaNet (SSM), 16 layers use full attention"). Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 40 layers = 30 linear + 10 full. Layers also carry attn_output_gate true (output_gate_type "swish") on full-attention layers; linear layers use short conv with linear_conv_kernel_dim 4. Native context max_position_embeddings 262144 ("262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,010,000" for 80B; Qwen3.5-Plus API ships 1M). MTP: mtp_num_hidden_layers 1 (one-layer nextn/MTP draft); vLLM maps model_type qwen3_5 / qwen3_5_text -> Qwen3_5MTP and qwen3_5_moe / qwen3_5_moe_text -> Qwen3_5MoeMTP with n_predict 1 (verified in local vLLM test tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py).
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: Yes - per-layer head-dim divergence inside one model, but by mechanism rather than by local/global variants of one mechanism: the 48 (or 36) linear-attention layers use 128-dim K/V heads while the 16 (or 12) full-attention layers use 256-dim heads. All full-attention layers share the identical (24 Q, 4 KV, 256) shape - there is no Gemma-style further split between local and global full-attention layers. A kernel stack must therefore cover BOTH d=256 paged KV attention AND d=128/128 Gated DeltaNet chunked/recurrent kernels for one model. Lineage note: the LMSYS blog (2026-08-26) states "The Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention hybrid design has been used from Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8", and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4 preview) keeps 3 GDN : 1 full-sparse pattern but replaces the full layer with QSA sparse attention (compression ratio 4, best 512 blocks).

kernel_support.supported_dims: Full attention d=256 on sm80+ is served by native template instantiation: vLLM's vendored FlashAttention supports head_size <= 256 (local file vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py even carries FA4_HD256 paths in this fork), FlashInfer covers arbitrary head dims via runtime JIT/autotune, and TRTLLM-Gen/TRTLLM_MHA serve it on Blackwell. Linear attention d=128/128 is served by Triton chunked kernels from flash-linear-attention (FLA) - generic and autotuned, no per-shape templates - plus vendor kernels added later: FlashInfer CUTLASS prefill (SM90), CuteDSL decode (SM90/100), Gluon prefill (SM100), with GDN state laid out [N, HV, V, K] (K-last; changed from [N, HV, K, V] in SGLang #20283). llama.cpp serves the same shapes under GGUF architecture "qwen35" [uncertain - exact general.architecture string inferred from the "unknown model architecture: 'qwen35'" error reports and llama.cpp conversion/qwen.py, not directly inspected] with a new FULL_ATTENTION_INTERVAL metadata key (conversion script default 4; PR #19468 merged after Qwen3.5 launch, tracked via issue #15940 / 'Qwen3.5 Support Merged in llama.cpp').
kernel_support.capability_gate: vLLM gates its FLASH_ATTN V1 backend at capability >= (8,0) - verified in the local tree (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py, per turing_lab/thirdparty/flashinfer-sm75-validation.md); FLASHINFER is gated the same way in vLLM (citing flashinfer #3620). So for this model family the d=256 layers never reach FlashAttention on Turing at all; the gate exists because vendored FA2's sm80+ kernels (cp.async, d=256 smem/register tiling) were never built or CI'd for sm_75. Standalone FlashInfer 0.6.18 DOES pass correctness on sm_75 for d=128 (local validation 2026-09-05: prefill and decode max_err <= 0.00094), but its d=256 path on sm_75 is unvalidated [uncertain]. Upstream FlashAttention-2 itself supports headdim 256 only on Ampere+; its Turing ceiling is commonly cited as 128 [uncertain - not directly verified this session].
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: On sm_75, vLLM V1 silently auto-selects TRITON_ATTN (generic Triton attention that accepts arbitrary head dims, including 256, at reduced performance) - FLASH_ATTN/FLASHINFER are simply not offered rather than erroring. In vLLM/SGLang the GDN layers always run FLA-style Triton (or vendor CuteDSL/Gluon on sm90+), wrapped by full CUDA graphs because Triton launch overhead disproportionately hurts decode batches (vLLM blog). No padding trick is needed at d=256 on sm80+ since 256 is a native template; unsupported shapes in FlashAttention raise errors rather than silently degrading. llama.cpp older builds fail hard with "unknown model architecture: 'qwen35'".
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: Upstream CI exercises sm80/sm90/sm100/sm120 (SGLang tracking issue #18590 items name SM90 CUTLASS prefill, SM90/100 CuteDSL, SM100 Gluon, SM120 XQA/FlashInfer, Blackwell TRTLLM_MHA/NVFP4); nothing in the vLLM/SGLang Qwen3.5 support trail mentions sm_75/Turing. The claim that Qwen3.5-family models run at all on Turing rests on out-of-tree effort: this project's local validation (FlashInfer sm_75 correctness at d=128, vLLM bridge work) and llama.cpp community runs on RTX 3080/6000. Coverage of 'supported' claims is actively drifting toward newest hardware (Blackwell-first kernels land while sm_75 stays untested).

performance.turing_baseline: No published vLLM/SGLang Turing numbers for Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 exist - official kernels target sm80+ and vendors benchmark B200/B300/H200 (e.g. LMSYS: 540 tok/s decode at TP4 on B200, bs=1, with MTP, accept length 3.3, for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4). Community Turing/Ampere-consumer-class data points are llama.cpp-only [uncertain - second-hand community reports, no controlled benchmarks]: Qwen3.8-27B GGUF fits 16GB VRAM on an RTX 3080 with quantization (autodidacts.io), ~17GB RAM/VRAM claim (unsloth.ai), and a DFlash2 speculative-decoding 'up to 4x' report on a rented RTX 6000 (Reddit r/LocalLLM, llama.cpp pr #27342). Nearest local measured anchor is the project's sm_75 FlashInfer decode microbench at d=128 (19.8 tok/s b=1 kv=1024 -> 6.4 tok/s kv=16384), which characterizes the kernel class, not this model.
performance.d256_feasibility: For the model: d=256 full attention is proven feasible and mainstream on sm80+ - it is the default of the highest-volume open-weight family. The design deliberately pairs 256 with very few KV heads (2 on 80B, 4 on 27B) and partial RoPE so cost stays low. For a Turing kernel: d=256 is achievable but not free - a bf16 K tile of 128 tokens x 256 dims is 64KB, which alone saturates Turing's 64KB shared-memory budget before V is staged, so a native-d=256 template must shrink the token tile while k-chunking (route B) reuses the proven d=128 pipeline. Only 1 of 4 layers needs it, and with 4 KV heads the GEMM shapes are skinny, so the win from a bespoke template is bounded. The GDN linear layers (128/128) are already covered by Triton FLA kernels that run anywhere.
performance.cost_analysis: KV memory: full layers only store 2*4*256 = 2048 elements/token/layer (27B) x 16 layers vs a hypothetical 64 full layers of a dense Qwen3-27B at 2*8*128 = 2048 - i.e. the hybrid cuts KV-layer count 4x (16 of 64 layers), which is why the hybrid is marketed as making long context cheap (DGX Spark notes: KV cache 'nearly free'; only ~25% of layers keep a real KV cache). Linear-attention state is fixed-size per layer independent of context: GDN state shape [N, HV, V, K] = 48 V-heads * 128 * 128 elements/layer (27B) plus conv state of width 6144 x kernel 4. Compute: 75% of layers cost O(1) per token in sequence length; the 25% full layers run d=256 GQA with head_dim**-0.5 scaling (1/16) and 6:1 group sharing, so per-layer QK^T FLOPs are 24*256 = 6144 wide on Q against only 4*256 = 1024 wide on K/V. Kernel budgets at d=256 on sm_75: accumulator registers per thread roughly double vs d=128 for the same tile shape, and smem forces tile reduction (see d256_feasibility). Compile-time/instantiation cost: FA2 needs a headdim-256 instantiation (sm80+ already ships one); a route-B chunked path pays a second pass over K plus an online-softmax rescale. MTP economics: the single MTP layer (mtp_num_hidden_layers 1, mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings false) is supported natively by vLLM (multi-token decode, no app changes) and by SGLang SpecV2/MTP spec_v2 for qwen3next/Qwen3.5 (tracking issue #18590; avoiding SSM/conv state copies in spec decoding reported up to ~9.47% e2e gain, on hold due to radix-cache conflict). Context cost: 262,144 native on open checkpoints (Qwen3.5-Plus API 1M; 80B extensible to 1,010,000) is practical only because 75% of layers hold constant-size state.

design_fit.route: Informs all three routes. Route A (native d=256 template): justified as the target shape because d=256-with-2..4-KV-heads is now the default full-attention shape of the dominant open family - but its smem footprint on sm_75 forces small token tiles, so a full template is the expensive path. Route B (k-chunked 256 on the 128 pipeline): attractive precisely because the workload is 25% of layers, 4 skinny KV heads, decode-dominated; reusing the proven d=128 tiles with a K split avoids a 64KB+ smem tile. Route C (bridge headers so unmodified FA2/FlashInfer serve the layer): FlashInfer already passes sm_75 correctness at d=128 (local validation) and JITs generic shapes, making it the first thing to test at d=256 before any custom kernel; FA2 itself is unreachable on sm_75 in vLLM (backend gated >= sm80).
design_fit.recommendation: Treat the Qwen3.5 lineage shape - full attention d=256 (partial RoPE 0.25, GQA 6:1 or 8:1) + GDN 128/128 in a 3:1 pattern - as the primary next target set for the sm_75 bridge, over exotica like Gemma-4's 512. Concretely: (1) benchmark FlashInfer 0.6.18 single/multi-request decode and prefill at d=256, kv_heads=4 on sm_75 using the existing contract-correct paged harness (extend flashinfer-sm75-validation.md); (2) if FlashInfer d=256 passes and is fast enough, prefer route C and spend engineering only on a Triton/GDN story; (3) otherwise implement route B k-chunked 256-on-128 in the bridge, since a native d=256 sm_75 template (route A) has the worst effort/payoff ratio. Keep the GDN layers on FLA-style Triton kernels - they are head-shape-portable and CUDA-graph friendly.
design_fit.numerics_risks: Partial RoPE (25%, 64 of 256 dims, mrope_interleaved with mrope_section [11,11,10] for the multimodal wrapper) means kernels cannot assume whole-head rotary; q_norm/k_norm RMSNorm per 256-dim head and the swish attn_output_gate (gate fused with Q projection: q_gate split into q and gate, then swish-gated - vllm qwen3_next.py) must be preserved in any fused bridge path. For GDN, accumulation order is observable: SGLang explicitly preserves 'the reference FP32 accumulation order and bitwise-identical outputs' in their fused paths and changed state layout [N,HV,K,V]->[N,HV,V,K] (#20283), so a bridge-side reimplementation must match chunked-scan order. No attention softcap in this family. RoPE theta is large (1e7) for the 262k context - precision of sin/cos at high dims matters on FP16-only Turing paths (no BF16 on sm_75 is a known constraint of this project).
design_fit.demand_weighting: Very high. Qwen is the most-downloaded open-weight family and the Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 line makes the hybrid+256 design the DEFAULT for the flagship local-model size: Qwen3.6/3.8-27B dense (27.8B) targets 16-24GB consumer cards (RTX 3080/4090-class threads dominate the community response), while Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and 397B-A17B extend it to MoE. Every d=256 full-attention layer these models run on Turing must go through a bridge or Triton path, so the installed base of T4/2080Ti/RTX 6000-class cards used for local LLM inference benefits directly; conversely, cloud/datacenter users are on sm80+ where d=256 is already native, so the bridge work is purely a Turing-installed-base play. Secondary beneficiaries: llama.cpp (already supports qwen35) users prove the demand for 27B-class hybrid inference on old GPUs; vLLM/SGLang currently route such users to TRITON_ATTN silently.
